title: Gora v1: an agent-core and trust-first design for a durable, Sentinel-gated personal agent that lives natively in Telegram
positioning:
Gora puts Muse-grade trust where people already talk. It is a Claude Opus 5 agent that actually does things (email, calendar, reminders, verified research, long-running missions and watchers) and cannot act behind your back. Every side effect passes through Sentinel, a deterministic policy layer written in code that the model cannot talk to. Anything that sends, changes or deletes something arrives as a separate approval card showing the exact diff. Only the owner's own tap can resolve it (an HMAC-signed callback, never chat text). Cards offer Muse's grant scopes (once, this task, 24h, always for this recipient), and risk tiers, a trust ladder and digests keep approval fatigue down. Everything goes into a hash-chained ledger of what Gora read, did and plans to do. Every memory shows its source, and forgetting is real: the history epoch is rotated and crypto-shredded, not just hidden.

Against each competitor:
- Mira has 1.17M MAU but is wide and shallow: about 95% of its traffic runs on cheap open-weight models, it has no documented approval UX, audit log or memory viewer, group facts are visible to members, and only 1 in 250 users connects a tool. Gora wins on depth and trust, and connects tools at the moment they are needed with a payoff within 60 seconds.
- folk uses typed /approve and /yolo, signs people up on a web dashboard, publishes contradictory pricing, and its users call memory 'an undo problem'. Gora keeps everything inside Telegram (the Mini App holds the ledger, memory and permissions), with approvals that cannot be spoofed and per-fact forgetting.
- Muse is US-only, 18+, requires a card, is 1:1 only, has opaque inferences and data-grab suggestions, and suffers from approval fatigue. Gora is global, needs no card and takes payment in Stars. Its proactive engine has a budget and must say why now. It also uses 2026 Telegram features none of these three fully exploit: stoppable streaming drafts, private-chat topics as durable task workspaces, Chat Automation commitment tracking with per-chat consent, and @gora guest mode in any chat.

Reliability is the product. Durable SQLite state, leases, tool_use_id idempotency and reconciliation mean a mission that waits six hours for your tap survives deploys and never double-sends.

v1_features.name: Zero-setup first five minutes (no card, no dashboard)
v1_features.user_story: As a new user I tap /start, or arrive through a deep link from a group or a guest mention. Within about 20 seconds I get a useful streamed answer to 'what is on your plate this week?' and a first reminder in the right timezone. I can name my agent and, if I want, import what ChatGPT or Claude knows about me. Gora offers to connect Google only when it unlocks something, and that connection pays off within 60 seconds.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: On /start, greet the user by first_name and infer the language from language_code. Ask one question with 4 inline chips, or let them send a voice note. Stream the answer with sendRichMessageDraft(can_stop:true), then finalize with sendRichMessage. Naming and style chips ([Gora][Scout][Nova][Custom], [Warm][Concise][Professional]) are stored on users and injected through the per-turn context message, never the static system prompt. Memory import: the user pastes text, messages.parse with zodOutputFormat extracts facts, and a card shows up to 8 facts with ✓/✗ callbacks. Timezone comes from the Mini App's Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone, or from a request_location reply-keyboard button resolved with geo-tz. Onboarding ends by pointing at the Mini App menu button (setChatMenuButton MenuButtonWebApp), whose Ledger already shows everything done so far.
v1_features.why_better: Muse needs a Meta account, a US location and a payment card. folk sends Telegram users through a web dashboard. Mira needs no setup, but only 1 in 250 of its users ever connects a tool. Gora delivers value before any connection and asks for access only at the moment it unlocks something.

v1_features.name: Stoppable streaming chat with honest status
v1_features.user_story: As a user I watch Gora's answer appear live and can press Stop at any time. During tool calls I see what it is doing ('Checking your calendar…'). I never read 'Done!' about something that is actually still waiting for my approval.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: Each run uses sendRichMessageDraft with one stable non-zero draft_id and can_stop:true. A <tg-thinking> status line is re-sent every 15 s or less so the 30 s draft never expires, and updates are throttled to at most 1 per 700 ms. The final message goes out with sendRichMessage (Rich Markdown). If that fails, fall back to telegram-md-entities {text, entities}, then to plain-text chunks. Update.stopped_message_generation aborts the Anthropic stream through the run's AbortController, and the partial text is kept as a real message marked '⏹ Stopped'. The state footer ('⏳ 1 action awaiting your approval ↓') is rendered from DB state, never from model text. Any <tg-button> tags the model emits are stripped. Voice notes are downloaded with getFile and sent to Groq whisper-large-v3-turbo with filename voice.ogg, and the transcript is echoed back. setMessageReaction 👀 acknowledges receipt.
v1_features.why_better: Muse overclaimed, saying it could haggle on Marketplace, and Poke is slow and silent. In Gora, status and completion claims come from deterministic ledger state, and Stop really cancels both the model call and any pending tool work.

v1_features.name: Sentinel approval cards with scoped grants and a trust ladder
v1_features.user_story: As a user, whenever Gora wants to send, change or delete something, I get a separate card showing exactly what will happen: recipient, subject, full body, calendar slot, and warnings such as 'this address came from an email, not from you'. One tap approves it once, for 24 hours, for this task, or always for this recipient. I can edit before approving. Nothing I type in chat and nothing the model writes can approve on my behalf.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics:
The card is a separate sendRichMessage generated by code, not by the model. It has the header '🔐 Approve: …', a GFM table diff and a <details> body. Inline keyboard, with button styles success or danger:
- [✅ Approve] [✖ Deny]
- [✏️ Edit], a web_app button that opens the Mini App approval page (DM only), and [⏱ 24h]
- [♾ Always for alice@x.com], shown only when eligible after 2 identical approvals
callback_data is 'a1:<id10>:<verb>:<scope>:<mac8>' (truncated HMAC-SHA256, 64 bytes or less). It is accepted only when callback_query.from.id is the owner. An atomic pending→approved UPDATE makes double taps no-ops. answerCallbackQuery is always called. The card is edited in place to its final state ('✅ Sent 14:04 · ledger #812'). Interactive approvals expire after 24 h. Low-risk mission approvals are batched into one digest card at the user's chosen time. Pending approvals are also listed in /approvals and in the Mini App.
v1_features.why_better: folk uses typed /approve and /yolo, which can be spoofed and are all-or-nothing. Mira's approval flow is undocumented. Muse's throughput is capped by how often you check your phone. Gora reproduces Muse's out-of-band, 5-scope model inside Telegram and reduces fatigue with risk tiers, a trust ladder and digests. Taint and provenance rules stop an 'always' grant from being exploited by injected content.

v1_features.name: Missions: durable background tasks in their own topic
v1_features.user_story: As a user I say 'find a dentist near work taking new patients next week and hold a slot in my calendar'. Gora opens a mission and works on it for minutes or days. It pauses for approvals or outside changes, survives restarts, and reports back in one tidy thread with a live status card and a Stop button.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: mission_start calls createForumTopic(chat_id=user, name, icon_color) to open a private-chat topic (Threaded Mode). If getMe().has_topics_enabled is false, the mission falls back to the main DM with a status card. The status card is a sendRichMessage task list, updated with editMessageText(rich_message). The mission run parks through task_wait (on a timer, an approval, a watcher or a user message) and the scheduler wakes it. Each mission has a cost budget; when it runs out, a card offers [Add budget] and [Stop]. On completion, editForumTopic renames the topic to '✅ …', a summary is posted, and a short notice goes to the DM. A [⏹ Stop] callback cancels the mission, and /tasks lists all missions.
v1_features.why_better: Muse's background tasks report back only when something changes, and only in a separate app. folk's watchers are paid and opaque, and Mira caps triggers at 10. Gora shows live progress that you can inspect in the ledger. Missions are built on write-ahead state, leases and reconciliation, so a 6-hour wait for approval survives deploys and never double-sends.

v1_features.name: Watchers that speak only on change
v1_features.user_story: As a user I ask Gora to watch a page, a price, a flight search or my inbox for a condition ('tell me if ALA→IST drops under $250', 'tell me when the visa page changes'). I hear from it only when the condition is met, and I see the before and after.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: watcher_create adds a recurring jobs row with jittered intervals (croner, IANA timezone). Each check is deterministic, through SentinelFetch or the Kiwi MCP search-flight. The content hash is compared first, and LLM extraction runs only when the hash changes. When the condition is met, Gora either sends a nudge card with the diff and [Open][Stop watching][Snooze], or wakes the mission that owns the watcher. Low-priority alerts use disable_notification. After 5 consecutive failures the watcher pauses and notifies the user. Free plans get 3 active watchers; paid plans get more.
v1_features.why_better: folk's watchers are paywalled and 1:1 only. Mira's triggers are capped at 10 and hard to find. About 30% of Poke's nudges are noise. Gora's watchers are cheap because they compare hashes first, explain what changed, and never speak without a change.

v1_features.name: Reminders and check-ins with deterministic time
v1_features.user_story: As a user I say 'remind me Tuesday at 3 to call mom'. Gora confirms 'Tue 14 Oct, 15:00 Almaty time' with a tappable date, fires on time even after restarts, and lets me snooze or mark it done with one tap.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: The time_resolve tool parses dates with chrono-node in the user's stored IANA zone; the model never does its own date arithmetic. It writes reminders and jobs rows. The confirmation uses a date_time entity (<tg-time unix=… format=wDT>), which the user can tap to add to their calendar. Reminders fire through the outbox with [✅ Done][⏰ 10 min][⏰ Tomorrow]. Recurring reminders use croner with DST-safe timezones. The timezone is resolved in this order: Mini App device timezone, then a shared location via the geo-tz default entry, then a typed city via Open-Meteo geocoding. It is always echoed back to the user.
v1_features.why_better: Poke's top complaints are wrong time zones and late reminders. Reminders are only 2% of Mira's usage. Gora computes time in code and shows its work.

v1_features.name: Ledger: everything Gora read, did and plans to do
v1_features.user_story: As a user I can open a timeline of every tool call, data read, approval, message sent and memory change. I can see what is scheduled or pending next. I can reply /why to any Gora message to learn which memories, sources and tools produced it.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: The executor, Sentinel and the approval service write the ledger rows, which are hash-chained and append-only. /ledger shows the last 10 entries as a rich table. The Mini App Ledger tab (with an initData-authenticated API) adds filters and a Planned section covering jobs, watchers, pending approvals and active missions. /why, sent as a reply to a bot message, maps tg_links to the run and then to llm_calls, tool_calls and run_memory_uses. It answers deterministically, so no LLM is needed to list the facts.
v1_features.why_better: Muse has an audit log, but its inferences are opaque and it fabricated an explanation for its Messages sync. folk's memory 'brain' lives on a web dashboard. Mira and Poke have no audit log. Gora's ledger lives inside Telegram, and every claim links to its source.

v1_features.name: Memory with provenance, consent and real forgetting
v1_features.user_story: As a user I see what Gora remembered and where each fact came from. I approve anything sensitive before it is stored. When I say 'forget what I said about my old job', it is truly gone. I can go incognito for an hour, and I can export or delete everything.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: Memory lives in structured memory_facts rows with scope, kind, sensitivity, confidence and source message. Facts are extracted after turns with messages.parse and zodOutputFormat. Instead of sending a new message, Gora adds a [📝 Remembered 2 · Review] button to its last message via editMessageReplyMarkup. Sensitive facts need a ✓ before they are saved. memory_forget does three things: it tombstones the fact, records forgotten fingerprints so the fact is never re-learned, and rotates the epoch so the text leaves the replayed Claude context. Commands: /memory, /forget, /incognito, /export (a JSON file through the Mini App's downloadFile) and /delete_me. Each fact can be edited or forgotten in the Mini App. Group and business facts live in separate scopes that never reach DM retrieval.
v1_features.why_better: folk's users call its memory 'an undo problem'. Mira's group facts are visible to members and it has no memory viewer. Muse's memory cannot be disabled, and it trains on user data by default. Gora offers per-fact provenance, consent for sensitive data and crypto-shredded forgetting, and it never trains on user data.

v1_features.name: Just-in-time integrations with a per-app permission matrix
v1_features.user_story: As a user, when I ask something that needs my Gmail or Calendar, Gora offers a Connect button right there. Within 60 seconds of connecting, it shows me one genuinely useful thing and tells me exactly what it read. For each app I choose whether Gora may only read, may also create drafts, or may propose sends and changes.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: Integration tools are always declared, so the toolset stays static and cache-friendly. When an app is not connected, the executor returns not_connected and sends a card with a url button. The button points to the Composio Connect Link from session.authorize(toolkit, {callbackUrl: https://<domain>/oauth/callback?state=…}). The callback sends a DM saying 'Connected ✓', with permission chips [Read only][Read + drafts][Can propose sends]; the default is read plus drafts. A first-look job reads the last 48 h of unanswered important mail and tomorrow's calendar, lists exactly what it read, and posts one approval card with a drafted fix. The Mini App Permissions tab changes levels and revokes grants and connections. The model has no way to change permissions.
v1_features.why_better: Mira admits only 1 in 250 users connects Gmail or Calendar. Muse's first inbox scan felt like a data grab. folk sends Telegram users to a web dashboard. Gora connects in context, tells you what it read, and defaults to the least privilege.

v1_features.name: Inbox and calendar actions done safely
v1_features.user_story: As a user I say 'tell Alice I'm 10 minutes late' or 'move my 3pm with Bob to tomorrow morning'. Gora drafts the exact email or picks the exact new slot after checking conflicts. I approve, it happens exactly once, and I can undo it where possible.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: Emails use a two-phase send. gmail_create_draft is allowed at the draft level, so the draft is visible in Gmail right away. gmail_send_draft is gated by an approval card. calendar_find_free_slots runs before calendar_create_event or calendar_update_event. tool_use_id is the idempotency key. After a crash, reconcile() searches Sent mail or events. If the outcome is still 'unknown', Gora asks the user instead of sending again. Tone is matched to the recipient, so there is no lowercase casual writing in outbound mail. New calendar events get a 10-minute [Undo] button.
v1_features.why_better: folk's casual tone makes users unwilling to let it send email. Muse slows users down with approval fatigue. Mira's actions are shallow Composio calls without an approval UX. Exact-diff approvals and reconciliation make it safe to hand Gora your outbound communication.

v1_features.name: Proactive suggestions on a budget, with a reason
v1_features.user_story: As a user I get at most N unprompted messages a day (3 by default). Each one says why now and what it is based on, with one-tap Do it, Snooze or Never this kind. Gora learns what I don't want.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: The proactive engine scores candidates from several signals: calendar conflicts, unanswered important mail (via Composio triggers), commitments coming due, watcher hits, birthdays in memory, and weather against outdoor events. The budget and quiet hours (default 22:00–08:00 local) are enforced in code. Each nudge card states why now, links its source, and offers [Do it][Snooze][Never this kind]. A 👎 reaction, received as a message_reaction update, counts as negative feedback. Low-priority nudges use disable_notification. The morning brief is optional and previewed during onboarding. /nudges and /quiet control the engine. The engine cannot ask for new data unless that data serves a goal the user stated.
v1_features.why_better: About 30% of Poke's nudges are noise. Muse's suggestions read as data grabs. folk has a nudge budget, but it sits behind commands. Gora budgets, explains and learns, and every control is one tap.

v1_features.name: Secretary Mode: commitments and approved replies in your real chats
v1_features.user_story: As a user who connects Gora under Settings > Chat Automation, I choose which chats Gora may read. It tracks promises I make ('I'll send it tomorrow'), flags messages I haven't answered, and drafts replies in my voice. Nothing goes out until I approve it.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: The business_connection update is stored with its rights and is_enabled flag. Each chat is opted in separately, through the '/start bizChat<user_chat_id>' deep link or the Mini App, and an explicit ToS 5.4(iv) consent card must be accepted before any content reaches Claude. Until then Gora stores only metadata (chat id and last incoming time). Messages from the owner (from.id == connection.user.id) go through commitment detection and become self-reminders. Messages from the other person are classified for 'needs reply' and can trigger a budgeted nudge with [Draft reply]. The draft appears as an approval card in the owner's DM. Approved text is sent with business_connection_id only if rights.can_reply is set and the chat had an incoming message within 24 h; otherwise the card offers a copy_text button. sender_business_bot is used to ignore Gora's own sends. deleted_business_messages removes the stored content. Every business read, draft and send is recorded in the ledger.
v1_features.why_better: Muse only knows your connected apps, and folk only sees its own chat. Mira offers business delegation without documented approvals. Gora sees the chats where decisions actually happen, with per-chat consent, draft-only defaults and full disclosure, all of which Telegram's ToS requires anyway.

v1_features.name: @gora guest help in any chat, without leaking your life
v1_features.user_story: As a user in any group or private chat I type '@gora what's a fair split of this bill?', or reply to a message with '@gora fact-check this', and get one clean answer. If the question needs my private data or a longer task, I get a button to continue privately.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: Update.guest_message is answered with exactly one answerGuestQuery(guest_query_id, InlineQueryResultArticle with InputRichMessageContent). If the answer takes more than 3 s, Gora answers with a placeholder immediately and finishes with editMessageText(inline_message_id, rich_message). Guest mode uses only the PUBLIC toolset: web_search, web_fetch, time_resolve, fx_convert, weather_get and place_verify. It never reads or writes memory and never touches integrations. The guest text and the replied-to text are labeled untrusted. A 'Continue privately' url button (t.me/<bot>?start=g_<token>) carries the request into the DM. Guest conversations are deleted after 24 h.
v1_features.why_better: Mira's group facts leak across members, and TeleClaw is a Q&A bot with no private continuation. Gora is useful in any chat but structurally cannot reveal private memory there, and every mention is a path into the private agent.

v1_features.name: Kill switch, data rights and Stars plans (trust never paywalled)
v1_features.user_story: As a user I can /pause all actions instantly and can export or delete everything. I can pay in Stars for more missions, watchers and usage. Approvals, the ledger, memory controls and deletion stay free forever.
v1_features.telegram_mechanics: /pause makes Sentinel deny every non-read tool and parks missions. /export builds a JSON bundle delivered through the Mini App's downloadFile, with Content-Disposition and Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to https://web.telegram.org. /delete_me asks for confirmation, revokes Composio connections, crypto-shreds the user's DEK and deletes their rows within 24 h. Plans are sold through createInvoiceLink(currency XTR, subscription_period 2592000) and opened with openInvoice. pre_checkout_query is answered in the control lane within 10 s without calling the LLM. successful_payment and Update.subscription (active, canceled or failed) update entitlements. /paysupport and /terms are available, and the Mini App shows a usage meter.
v1_features.why_better: Muse requires a card even on its Free tier and is US-only. Mira sells opaque token packs. folk's pricing contradicts itself across its own pages. Gora is global, needs no card, takes payment inside Telegram, and keeps safety features free.

architecture:
GORA v1 ARCHITECTURE (agent-core and trust first)

==============================================================
0. PRINCIPLES
==============================================================
- P1. The model proposes; code disposes.
  - Every side effect is a ToolSpec, and only tools/executor.ts runs it, after sentinel.evaluate().
  - The model has no tool that can approve, grant, raise a permission, change an integration's scopes, or message an arbitrary Telegram chat.
- P2. Write-ahead durability.
  - Every state transition is committed to SQLite before the external effect happens, so any restart can resume any run.
  - The idempotency key for a side effect is the Claude tool_use_id. Every side-effecting ToolSpec implements reconcile().
- P3. Append-only history.
  - messages rows hold the exact API content JSON (encrypted). They are never updated or deleted, and SQLite triggers enforce this.
  - The only way to 'change' history is to start a new epoch: a client-side 'simple compaction' made of a summary plus a new user turn. This follows Claude's preserved-thinking rules, so moving to claude-opus-5-5 later is a config change.
- P4. One frozen prompt prefix for everyone.
  - Top-level system is one static block. Tools are name-sorted, with JSON Schema generated from zod and snapshot-tested.
  - Both are byte-identical across users, which gives a cross-user 1h cache.
  - Everything personal or time-varying goes into appended role:'system' context messages.
- P5. Mock-first.
  - Every external dependency sits behind a contract with a Fake.
  - The whole product runs in vitest with a fake Telegram (a grammY recording transformer), scripted Claude, in-memory SQLite and a FakeClock.
- P6. Degrade, never break. Feature flags come from getMe and from error responses: topics, guest mode, business mode, rich messages, role:'system' support and beta headers.

==============================================================
1. RUNTIME TOPOLOGY (one Node 26 process)
==============================================================
main.ts builds everything with createApp(deps) and starts `node src/main.ts`. The code is erasable-only TypeScript run through type stripping, and typescript@7 is used only for `tsc --noEmit`.

Components:
- HTTP (hono 4.13 + @hono/node-server 2.1). Routes:
  - POST /tg/webhook: checks X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token, inserts into inbox, returns 200 in under 50 ms.
  - /api/*: the Mini App JSON API, authenticated with initData.
  - GET /oauth/callback: return from Composio Connect.
  - POST /hooks/composio: signed triggers.
  - /app/*: the static Vite build.
  - /healthz and /metrics.
- UpdateSource.
  - WebhookSource in production: setWebhook(url, {secret_token, allowed_updates: EXPLICIT_LIST, max_connections: 40}).
  - PollingSource in development: getUpdates long-poll with timeout 30 and the offset persisted in kv.
  - Both call inbox.accept(update), which is an INSERT OR IGNORE on update_id.
  - EXPLICIT_LIST = message, edited_message, callback_query, guest_message, stopped_message_generation, business_connection, business_message, edited_business_message, deleted_business_messages, pre_checkout_query, subscription, my_chat_member, message_reaction.
- Dispatcher. It drains inbox and routes each update to a lane.
  - CONTROL lane, run immediately and concurrently: callback_query, stopped_message_generation, pre_checkout_query, subscription, business_connection, deleted_business_messages, message_reaction.
  - CONVERSATION lanes: keyed by scope_key and run serially through an in-process keyed mutex.
  - Handlers only persist input and enqueue runs or jobs, finishing in under 200 ms. They never call the LLM.
- RunWorker pool.
  - Async concurrency 32. At most 1 interactive run per conversation and at most 3 mission runs per user.
  - Runs are claimed with a lease (lease_until = now + 120 s, renewed every 30 s while streaming).
- Scheduler. A single timer sleeps until the next due job (1 s at most) and claims jobs with leases. croner computes recurrences in IANA timezones.
- Outbox worker.
  - Durable Telegram sends with per-chat token buckets: 1 msg/s in private chats, 20/min in groups, 25/s globally.
  - Honors 429 retry_after and backs off on 5xx. @grammyjs/auto-retry is installed on bot.api as the inner retry.
- Boot.
  1. Open the DB with WAL, busy_timeout 5000, foreign_keys ON and secure_delete ON, then run migrations.
  2. Call getMe, or use a fixed botInfo in tests. Derive flags from has_topics_enabled, supports_guest_queries, can_connect_to_business and has_main_web_app, and log any that are disabled.
  3. Recover state:
     - inbox rows in 'processing' go back to 'new'.
     - Runs with expired leases are reclaimed.
     - tool_calls in 'executing' are reconciled.
     - Jobs in 'running' are rescheduled.
  4. Call setMyCommands and setChatMenuButton(MenuButtonWebApp), then start the sources.
- Shutdown on SIGTERM.
  - Stop the sources.
  - Abort in-flight streams: the runs go back to queued, and their drafts simply expire.
  - Drain the outbox for 5 s, then close the DB.

==============================================================
2. MODULE LAYOUT
==============================================================
src/
  main.ts, config.ts (zod env schema and feature flags)
  contracts/ (written first; every workstream codes against these)
    llm.ts: LlmTransport { stream(req, handlers, signal): Promise<BetaMessage>; parse<T>(req, schema): Promise<{parsed: T|null, usage}> }
    telegram.ts: TelegramGateway, the subset of grammY Api used; ReplyChannel
    tools.ts: ToolSpec<I> { name; description (says WHEN to call); schema (zod); actionClass read|self|draft|write|send|delete|memory|control; risk 0-4; integration?; toolset FULL|PUBLIC; taintsRun; targets(input); renderDiff(input); statusLabel(input); execute(ctx, input, idem); reconcile?(ctx, input, idem) }
    sentinel.ts: evaluate(ProposedAction, SentinelSnapshot): Decision {kind allow|deny|ask, ruleId, reason, risk, grantId?, warnings[]}
    integrations.ts: IntegrationProvider {connectLink, execute, revoke, listConnections}
    capabilities.ts: SpeechToText, TimezoneResolver, WeatherProvider, FlightSearch, PlaceVerifier, Clock, Crypto, Fetch (injected)
  kernel/: clock, ulid ids, crypto (AES-256-GCM envelope + HMAC), pino log with redaction, errors
  db/: sqlite.ts (node:sqlite DatabaseSync, tx helper using BEGIN IMMEDIATE), migrations/*.sql (including append-only triggers), repos/*.ts (typed repositories; the only place SQL lives)
  telegram/: bot.ts (createBot({token, botInfo, transformers})), ingress.ts (inbox, sources), dispatcher.ts (lanes), handlers/ (message, voice, callback, stop, guest, business, payments, commands, location), render/ (markdown sanitize and fallback chain, cards.ts, callbackData.ts), channels/ (DmStreamChannel, NotifyChannel, BusinessChannel, GuestChannel), draftStreamer.ts, outbox.ts, topics.ts
  agent/: prompt/system_v1.ts (frozen text + version), prompt/context.ts (per-turn role:'system' builder), toolset.ts (FULL and PUBLIC frozen lists, tools_hash), requestBuilder.ts, loop.ts (stepRun), runs.ts (claim, lease, park, wake), stopReasons.ts, fallbackEcho.ts, epochs.ts (rotation and seed summaries), routes.ts (model and effort per route), sanitizeOutput.ts
  tools/: executor.ts (the ONLY caller of ToolSpec.execute), builtin/ (time, memory, reminders, missions, watchers, ledger, approvals-revise, settings, integration-connect), integrations/ (gmail, gcal, notion, todoist, drive over IntegrationProvider), research/ (place_verify, fx, weather, flight_search), business/ (draft_reply, commitment_track)
  sentinel/: sentinel.ts (pure rule engine), rules.ts (S01..S99), taint.ts, provenance.ts (trusted_targets), grants.ts, egress.ts (SentinelFetch host allowlists), redact.ts (OTP, magic-link and reset-link stripping, secret scrubbing), untrusted.ts (envelopes)
  approvals/: service.ts (create, render, resolve, expire, supersede, digest, trust ladder)

==============================================================
3. CONVERSATIONS AND SCOPE KEYS
==============================================================
Chat ids from guest and business updates are independent namespaces, so each conversation is keyed by a scope_key:
- dm:<tg_user_id>
- topic:<tg_user_id>:<thread_id> (a user-created topic)
- mission:<mission_id> (bound to a Gora-created topic)
- biz:<business_connection_id>:<chat_id>: owner-facing work about that business chat. Its outputs go to the owner's DM as cards.
- guest:<guest_query_id>: one-shot, deleted after 24 h.
- grp:<chat_id>: later.

Each conversation is frozen at creation:
- model (claude-opus-5)
- route, one of chat, mission, public, business
- effort: chat medium, mission high, public low, business medium
- toolset, FULL or PUBLIC
- tools_hash
- system_prompt_version
- epoch

Missions get their own conversation, so a different effort setting never churns another conversation's cache.

==============================================================
4. THE AGENT LOOP
==============================================================
4.1 Request build. Every call has this shape. Streaming is always on for the main loop.
  client.beta.messages.stream({
    model: conv.model,
    max_tokens: ROUTE.maxTokens,            // chat 32000, mission 64000, public 8000
    system: [{ type: 'text', text: SYSTEM_V1, cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral', ttl: '1h' } }],
    tools: TOOLSET[conv.toolset],           // name-sorted, frozen; hash must equal conv.tools_hash or the run fails fast
    messages: history,                      // concatenation of decrypted rows for (conv, epoch), nothing else
    thinking: { type: 'adaptive' },
    output_config: { effort: conv.effort },
    cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral', ttl: '1h' },   // top-level automatic tail breakpoint (longest TTL first is respected)
    fallbacks: 'default',                   // cast; typing for the scalar form is unconfirmed
    betas: BETAS,                           // ['server-side-fallback-2026-07-01'] + flag-gated 'mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21'
    metadata: { user_id: hmac(userId) }
  })
Notes on the request:
- FULL toolset:
  - Server tools: web_search_20260209 (max_uses 5, blocked_domains) and web_fetch_20260209.
  - Custom tools with eager_input_streaming:true only on the large-body tools: gmail_create_draft, business_draft_reply and notion_create_page.
- No code execution in v1. The docs warn against mixing it with the _20260209 web tools.
- Transport fallback: if the model returns 400 "role 'system' is not supported", the transport switches that model to a <\system-reminder> text block inside the user turn (flagged per model).

4.2 Run state machine.
  queued → running → (tool rounds) → running → done | refused | failed | cancelled
  running → parked (task_wait outstanding) → queued (on wake) → running
Only one active run per conversation. New inputs land in conversation_inputs.

4.3 stepRun(runId), in pseudocode:
  claim run (lease). If conv.rotate_pending, rotate the epoch first (4.9).
  If the last row is not an open tool round, consume all unconsumed conversation_inputs into ONE user message (text, image and document blocks), then append a context role:'system' message (4.8). Both are appended in one transaction.
  loop:
    req = build(conv)
    msg = await transport.stream(req, {onText → channel.onText, onBlockStart → channel.onBlockStart}, run.abort.signal)
      Errors, most specific first:
      - APIConnectionError / RateLimitError / InternalServerError / overloaded 529: after the SDK's 2 retries, requeue the run with not_before = now + backoff. After 60 s the user sees 'taking longer than usual'.
      - BadRequestError: fail the run, log request_id and the request diff, apologize, and alert.
      - Eager-input JSON parse error: re-issue the turn, at most 2 times.
    Insert llm_calls (usage, cache fields, usage.iterations, model served, fallback_used, stop_reason).
    Branch on stop_reason:
      refusal: check it FIRST and never read tool_use from a refused turn. Store the raw response only in llm_calls. Append a synthetic assistant text row with the friendly message we show. Run → refused.
      pause_turn: append the assistant content verbatim (after the echo transform) and continue. No 'Continue' message. At most 5 continuations.
      max_tokens with a tool_use present: never execute. Retry once from the same prefix with double max_tokens (cap 128000), with nothing appended. Otherwise fail.
      model_context_window_exceeded: set rotate_pending='context_exceeded', rotate, and retry.
      end_turn / stop_sequence / max_tokens without tools: append the assistant row, then channel.finalize(), then enqueue memory.extract (debounced 2 min). Run → done.
      tool_use:
        tx { append assistant row verbatim; insert tool_calls(staged) for each tool_use block in order }
        For each tool_use (reads run in parallel; side effects run sequentially in block order):
          parsed = spec.schema.safeParse(input). If invalid, the result is is_error with {INVALID_INPUT: …}.
          decision = sentinel.evaluate(action, snapshot). Always recorded in sentinel_decisions and the ledger.
            allow: tool_calls.status = executing (committed), then execute(ctx, input, idem = tool_use_id), then succeeded or failed. Output is redacted, wrapped as <untrusted source=…> when spec.taintsRun, and the run is marked tainted.
            deny: is_error result 'Blocked by Sentinel (rule S07: …). Do not retry; explain to the user.'
            ask: approvals.create(), which queues the card in the outbox. The result is NON-error: {status:'pending_approval', approval_id, summary, performed:false, instruction:'Tell the user it awaits their tap; never say it is done.'}
          task_wait: status = waiting. The run parks after the other tools finish.
        If any call is waiting: persist, set the run to parked with wake_on, return. Its tool_result is delivered at wake time.
        Otherwise: tx { append ONE user message = [all tool_result blocks in tool_use order] + an optional trailing text block with steering inputs (4.6) + a fresh context role:'system' message if clear_at is on or events arrived }, then continue.
  Server tool blocks (server_tool_use / web_search_tool_result) in assistant content also mark the run tainted.

4.4 Streaming into Telegram. Channels are chosen by conversation kind and trigger.
- DmStreamChannel (interactive DM or topic run). DraftStreamer is our own class of about 200 lines; @grammyjs/stream is not used, because one run spans several model calls and parks.
  - draft_id = a stable non-zero 31-bit int per run segment.
  - First call: sendRichMessageDraft(chat_id, draft_id, {markdown: '<tg-thinking>…</tg-thinking>'}, {message_thread_id, can_stop: true}).
  - Text deltas accumulate and pass through sanitizeOutput, which:
    - strips <tg-button>, <tg-button-row>, login_url and web_app tags;
    - closes unclosed code fences;
    - neutralizes any line imitating the '🔐 Approve' card header.
  - Throttled to at most 1 draft update per 700 ms, skipping intermediate states.
  - During tool execution the status line is statusLabel(input), re-sent every 15 s or less so the 30 s draft never dies.
  - Each segment ends with sendRichMessage({markdown: text + stateFooter}). stateFooter is rendered from DB state (pending approvals, parked mission) and never from model text.
  - On a 400 parse error, fall back to telegram-md-entities renderMarkdown + splitMessage via sendMessage(entities), then to plain 4096-char chunks.
  - tg_links records every message_id → (conversation, seq, run).
- NotifyChannel (background, mission and proactive runs). No drafts. The final text goes through the outbox, with disable_notification when low priority. Mission progress edits the status card.
- BusinessChannel. Never streams and never sends content directly. Everything becomes an approval card in the owner's DM (see 7.3).
- GuestChannel. See 7.4.

4.5 Stop.
- The in-memory map (chat_id, thread_id, draft_id) → run is also persisted in runs.draft_id.
- On stopped_message_generation (CONTROL lane):
  - run.abort, which aborts the Anthropic stream;
  - cancel tool_calls that have not started. An executing side effect is allowed to finish, because it is idempotent and recorded.
  - Append a synthetic assistant text row holding the visible partial text (no thinking or tool_use blocks, so history stays well-formed and append-only).
  - Send the partial text as a real message with '⏹ Stopped'. Run → cancelled.
  - The next context message notes that the previous reply was stopped by the user.
- If the stop arrives after the assistant row was persisted with tool_use blocks, the tool_calls get is_error 'Cancelled by user' results, appended on the next run, so the pairing stays valid.

4.6 Steering. A user message that arrives while a run is inside a tool round is appended as a trailing text block ('[User, 14:05]: …') after the tool_result blocks of the next tool-result user message; the docs allow a trailing text block there. Messages that arrive while the final answer is streaming wait for the next run. A message in a parked mission topic wakes the mission with reason user_input.

4.7 Fallback echo. At write time, fallbackEcho.ts drops thinking, redacted_thinking, tool_use and unpaired server_tool_use blocks that appear before the final 'fallback' block. The stored row is therefore byte-stable for replay, and tools are extracted only from the transformed content. The raw response is kept in llm_calls for audit. After a cyber-category decline, expect about 1 h of sticky routing to claude-opus-4-8 with a cold cache.

4.8 The per-turn context message: role:'system', appended after the user turn and never edited. It holds, compactly (300-800 tokens):
  <gora_context v=1>
    now: 2026-09-28T14:03+05:00 (Mon, Asia/Almaty, source miniapp)
    agent: name=Nova style=concise; user plan=free, quotas left
    conversation: dm | mission M-12 'ALA→IST fares' | business chat 'Aida' (owner-facing)
    integrations: gmail=draft, gcal=act, notion=not_connected
    memories: [m_12] …, [m_31] … (ids recorded in run_memory_uses)
    open: pending approvals [A7K2 send to alice@…], missions, next reminders
    events since last turn: A7K2 approved and sent 13:40; watcher W3 hit
    budget: nudges left 2
  </gora_context>
- With FEATURE_CLEAR_AT on, it is sent with clear_at:'next_user_message', and a fresh copy is re-appended after each tool-result message, so old copies cost 0 input tokens.
- With the flag off, it accumulates. Epoch rotation bounds the cost.

4.9 Epochs. One mechanism covers compaction, forgetting, prompt/tool upgrades and model switches.
- rotate(conv, reason):
  1. A side call writes a seed summary of the epoch with messages.parse. Instructions: keep profile facts, open tasks, pending approvals and commitments; EXCLUDE forgotten items, which are passed transiently.
  2. The summary is checked against forgotten_fingerprints.
  3. epoch+1 begins with ONE user message [seed text, then the new inputs].
  4. For a forget or a deletion, the old epoch is shredded: a shred_token is inserted and its rows are deleted with secure_delete.
- Triggers:
  - last_input_tokens > 120k (configurable);
  - forget requests;
  - a system_prompt_version or tools_hash bump, applied lazily at the next run;
  - a model change;
  - model_context_window_exceeded.
- Server compaction (compact_20260112) is behind a flag and off by default until its trigger config is verified.
- Keep-tail client compaction is never used, and rotation never happens mid tool round (the run must be idle).

4.10 Invariant tests run in CI on every e2e scenario:
- (a) Prefix stability: within an epoch, request k+1's messages start with exactly the bytes of request k's messages.
- (b) system and tools are byte-identical across all users and turns for a given version.
- (c) Every tool_use has exactly one tool_result in the immediately following user message.
- (d) No messages row is ever updated.
- An optional live-key CI job runs the block-binding beta with prefix_mismatch_behavior:'error' to catch history edits before any move to claude-opus-5-5.

==============================================================
5. SENTINEL AND APPROVALS
==============================================================
5.1 Sentinel.evaluate is a pure function over a snapshot: permissions, grants, trusted_targets, run taint, quotas, user status and the current time. Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins.
- S01: user paused → deny every non-read action.
- S02: tool not in this conversation's toolset or context → deny.
- S03: integration not connected → deny 'not_connected'. The executor converts this into a Connect card.
- S04: permission level below what the action needs (none < read < draft < act) → deny. The card links to the Mini App Permissions tab; only the user can change it there.
- S05: risk 4 (money, credentials, account security) → deny in v1.
- S06: quota or budget exceeded → deny. Examples: sends 20/day, calendar writes 30/day, mission cost cap.
- S07: business action without chat consent, without rights.can_reply, or outside the 24 h window → deny, with a copy_text fallback.
- S08: bulk action (more than 5 recipients or more than 10 items) → ask, and no grant applies.
- S09: risk 3 destructive action → ask with the exact diff; only 'once' is allowed.
- S10: any target not in trusted_targets (not from the user's own messages, user-sourced memory or a previously approved action) → ask with the warning '⚠ this recipient came from <source>, not from you'. No grant can cover it.
- S11: run tainted and the action is send or write → ask, unless a grant exists AND every target is user-trusted.
- S12: matching grant (once, task, ttl or always) → allow; a 'once' grant is consumed.
- S13: read, self or draft action within the permission level → allow, recorded in the ledger.
- S14: memory write in a sensitive category, or with no memory consent → ask (consent card).
- S99: anything else → ask.

Risk tiers:
- R0 read.
- R1 own-space and reversible: reminders, own-calendar events without attendees, todoist add, gmail draft, label changes.
- R2 outbound or shared: send email, invites, business replies, shared Notion pages.
- R3 destructive: delete event or mail, bulk operations.
- R4 money and credentials.

5.2 Approval lifecycle.
- create():
  - Store the exact validated input (payload_enc plus sha256), a card rendered from renderDiff(), warnings, targets and an expiry: 24 h when interactive, set by the mission (at most 7 days) for missions.
  - The outbox sends the card to the originating thread. Low-urgency R1/R2 mission approvals are held for the digest.
- Callback resolution (CONTROL lane):
  - Decode 'a1:<id10>:<verb>:<scope>:<mac8>'. Verify the HMAC over (id|verb|scope|owner_tg_id) and check callback_query.from.id == owner.
  - Run UPDATE pending_actions SET status='approved' … WHERE id=? AND status='pending'. It must change exactly 1 row; otherwise answer 'Already handled'.
  - Always call answerCallbackQuery.
  - If the scope is not 'once', create the grant.
  - Re-evaluate Sentinel with the approval as a one-shot grant, which re-checks /pause, permission revocations and quotas.
  - The executor runs the STORED payload (sha256 must match) with idem = tool_use_id.
  - editMessageText turns the card into its final state, for example '✅ Sent 14:04 · ledger #812', with [Undo] where a compensating action exists.
  - Write the ledger entry.
  - Wake parked runs whose wake_on includes approval:<id>, and queue an event for the next context message.
- There is no model call between approval and execution. What you approved is exactly what runs.
- Edit: [✏️ Edit] opens the Mini App approval page (web_app button, DM only). Edited fields are re-validated by zod and Sentinel and stored as edited_payload with a ledger diff.
- Revise by chat: the user replies to a card ('make it warmer'). tg_links maps the reply to the approval, and the model calls revise_pending_action, which supersedes the old card (edited to 'Superseded') and creates a new one.
- Trust ladder: after 2 approved actions with the same (tool, target) and no intervening denial, the next card shows [♾ Always for <target>]. It is never offered for R3, S08, S10 or business sends.
- Expiry job: expired approvals are auto-denied, the card is edited, and a parked mission gets 'expired'.
- Digest job: one card per digest time with per-item buttons. 'Approve all shown' is allowed only when every item is R1.

5.3 Taint and provenance.
- taint.ts collects the sources a run has seen: web results, email, Drive or Notion content, business messages, forwarded messages (forward_origin), guest or group text, and imported text.
- Taint carries from a run into the missions it spawns.
- trusted_targets is filled from email addresses and handles in the user's own messages (extracted deterministically), from memory facts whose source_kind is user_message, and from approved actions.

6. MISSIONS, WATCHERS AND SCHEDULER
==============================================================
- mission_start(title, goal, success_criteria, deadline?, budget_hint?):
  1. Sentinel quota check.
  2. Insert the missions row.
  3. createForumTopic(chat_id = user_id, name ≤ 128, icon_color from the allowed set). If topics are disabled, the mission lives in the DM with a '[M-12]' prefix.
  4. Create the conversation mission:<id>, bound to message_thread_id.
  5. Post the status card (sendRichMessage task list in the topic).
  6. Enqueue a run with trigger mission_start.
- Missions follow the prompt rule: plan, act, and park with task_wait instead of looping. mission_report edits the status card and optionally posts a message; posts are limited to 1 notifying message per mission per hour, except completion and approvals. mission_finish posts the summary, sends a short DM notice and calls editForumTopic('✅ ' + title).
- task_wait(until?, on: ['approval:<id>' | 'watcher:<id>' | 'user_input'], timeout) parks the run.
  - The scheduler job run.wake, or an event handler, calls wake(runId, reason, payload).
  - On wake, the task_wait tool_result becomes {woke_because, details} and is appended together with the other staged results in one user message, followed by a context message.
  - The run is then re-queued.
- Budget: missions.spent_micros is updated from llm_calls and tool costs. At the cap the mission parks with 'budget' and a card offering [Add budget][Stop].
- Watchers:
  - watcher.check jobs run on interval_s with ±10% jitter and fetch through SentinelFetch (GET only, host recorded) or FlightSearch.
  - Content is hashed first. Only a changed hash triggers extraction (deterministic extractor_json, or a side call with messages.parse), followed by the condition check.
  - A hit wakes the owning mission or sends a proactive nudge (budget-exempt, because the user asked for it).
  - 5 consecutive failures pause the watcher and notify the user.
- Scheduler.
  - Claim query: SELECT … FROM jobs WHERE status='scheduled' AND run_at<=now ORDER BY run_at LIMIT 50, followed by a conditional UPDATE that sets the lease.
  - Retries use exponential backoff with jitter up to max_attempts, then the job is marked dead and written to the ledger, with a user notice if it was user-facing.
  - Recurring jobs compute their next run_at with croner in the job's IANA tz. If a missed run is more than 2× the interval late, it is coalesced into one run.
  - Job kinds:
    - run.wake, reminder.fire, watcher.check
    - approval.expire, approval.digest
    - memory.extract, epoch.rotate
    - proactive.scan (per user, at user-local times), brief.morning
    - business.followup, commitment.due
    - mission.budget_check, subscription.reconcile, connection.health
    - first_look (runs after connect)
    - retention.sweep: inbox after 72 h, guest conversations after 24 h, business message content after 30 days, raw llm payload fields after 30 days.

7.3 Business (Secretary Mode).
- business_connection upserts business_connections (rights, is_enabled) and DMs the owner a setup card.
- business_message:
  - Before chat consent: store only last_incoming_at, last_owner_reply_at and unanswered_since, with no content.

- guest_message creates conversation guest:<guest_query_id> with the PUBLIC toolset and effort low.

  - Otherwise: answer with a placeholder ('…working'), keep inline_message_id, and finish with editMessageText(inline_message_id, rich_message).

==============================================================
8. MEMORY PIPELINE
==============================================================
- Retrieval, per run, from memory/retrieve.ts:
  - Decrypt the user's facts into a per-user LRU cache.
  - Pinned profile facts (up to 15), plus BM25 over the input text, plus a recency boost, plus person facts for names that are mentioned.
  - Filter by the allowed scopes: dm → user; biz → user (read) + biz:chat; guest → none.
  - Inject the fact ids and record them in run_memory_uses.
- Extraction, via the memory.extract job debounced per conversation:
  - A messages.parse call with zodOutputFormat({facts: [{text, kind, subject, sensitivity, confidence, source_seq, supersedes_id?}]}) over the new turns plus a digest of existing facts.
  - Drop candidates that match forgotten_fingerprints and anything written while incognito.
  - normal → active. sensitive → pending_consent.
  - editMessageReplyMarkup adds [📝 Remembered N · Review] to the last answer.
- memory_save: an explicit save by the user.
- Forget. memory_forget(ids | query):
  - In an untainted run with a direct user request: forget immediately and reply 'Forgot 3 memories'.
  - In a tainted run: ask first.
  - Either way: text_enc is nulled, the fingerprint (HMAC of normalized shingles) is recorded, rotate_pending='forget' is set on the affected conversations (rotated at the next idle point, within 5 minutes by job), and the ledger records it.
- Import: pasted export text → parse → a ✓/✗ card or Mini App list → source_kind import.
- Export: JSON containing facts with provenance, the ledger, reminders, missions and settings.

==============================================================
9. PROACTIVE ENGINE
==============================================================
- Signals: calendar tomorrow (evening scan), Composio mail triggers classified for importance, commitments due, watcher hits, dates in memory, and weather against outdoor events.
- score = value × confidence × timeliness × kind_weight. kind_weight is learned from Do it, Snooze, Never and 👎 reactions.
- Send when all of these hold: score > threshold, the daily budget has room (default 3; reminders, approvals and user-requested watcher hits don't count), the user is outside quiet hours and not paused.
- Otherwise the nudge is held for the morning brief or digest.
- Every nudge stores why_enc and a source_ref, and renders the why-now line.
- Nudges that ask for more data are limited to 1 per integration per 14 days, and only when a user-stated goal needs that data.

- plans.ts defines Free, Plus and Pro entitlements: turns/day, active missions, watchers, web searches, voice minutes, mission budget. The trust features are identical on every tier.
- createInvoiceLink({title, description, payload: 'plan:<plan>:v1:<userId>', currency: 'XTR', prices: [{label, amount}], subscription_period: 2592000}) creates the link, opened via openInvoice.
- pre_checkout_query is answered in the CONTROL lane by a pure check of payload and user, within 10 s.
- successful_payment → a payments row (telegram_payment_charge_id) and the subscription active until subscription_expiration_date.
- Update.subscription moves the state to active, canceled or failed.
- /paysupport and /terms are available. Admin tools cover refundStarPayment and editUserStarSubscription.
- meter.ts enforces quotas at run start (S06) and aggregates usage_daily from llm_calls.

==============================================================
12. DEPLOYMENT
==============================================================
- Dockerfile: node:26-slim. `npm ci && vite build miniapp`, CMD `node src/main.ts`.
- One VM or machine with a persistent volume (Fly.io machine + volume, or Hetzner), with TLS at the edge.
- Files and backups:
  - /data/gora.db is replicated with Litestream to S3. Contents are already field-encrypted.
  - /keys/keys.db sits on a separate secret volume with its own short-retention backup, so the key is stored separately from the data.
- Env: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, WEBHOOK_SECRET, PUBLIC_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GORA_KEK (or KEK_FILE), CALLBACK_HMAC_KEY, COMPOSIO_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, optional OPENAI_API_KEY/DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, MODEL_MAIN=claude-opus-5, MODEL_SIDE, FEATURE_* flags.
- BotFather checklist:
  - Turn on: Threaded Mode, Guest Mode, Secretary Mode, Main Mini App with the exact domain, menu button, Stars payments.
  - Leave Bot-to-Bot OFF in v1. Keep privacy mode ON.
- Observability: pino JSON logs with redaction (token, initData and message text are never logged). Metrics:
  - runs by state, TTFT, cache hit ratio = cache_read / (input + cache_read), cost per active user;
  - pending approvals and time-to-approve;
  - nudge acceptance;
  - activation, meaning the user connected a tool in session 1.

==============================================================
13. TESTING (no network, no keys)
==============================================================
Fakes:
- FakeTelegram: a grammY Bot with a fixed botInfo and a recording transformer installed FIRST, so autoRetry wraps it. Canned results: Message-like for send*, true for others, SentGuestMessage {inline_message_id}, ForumTopic for createForumTopic.
  - DSL: tg.userSends(text), tg.userSendsVoice(fixture), tg.userTaps(cardId, verb), tg.userPressesStop(), tg.businessMessage(…), tg.guestMention(…), tg.preCheckout(…).
- ScriptedLLM: a queue of scripted responses, each a sequence of stream events plus a final BetaMessage, with matchers on the request. It records every request for invariant checks and can simulate thinking blocks with signatures, parallel tool_use, pause_turn, pre- and mid-stream refusal, fallback blocks, max_tokens with a partial tool_use, 429/529/connection errors, and abort.
- FakeComposio, FakeSTT, FakeFetch (host-recorded), FakeClock (advance()), and ':memory:' or temp-file SQLite. The temp-file DB simulates restarts by creating a second app instance on the same file.

Golden e2e scenarios:
1. Stream and finalize, including the rich-parse fallback.
2. Email approval flow: approve executes exactly once, even with a double tap.
3. Forged callback_data or a wrong from.id is rejected.
4. A model-emitted <tg-button> is stripped.
5. Approval after 6 h across a restart, then execution.
6. A mission parks on a watcher, wakes and reports.
7. Stop aborts the run and keeps the partial text.
8. After a forget, the fact bytes are absent from every later recorded request.
9. Guest: one answerGuestQuery, then an inline edit.
10. Business: no LLM request ever contains content from a non-consented chat (asserted on ScriptedLLM).
11. Nudge budget and quiet hours.
12. Crash during an executing send → reconcile → 'unknown' → the user is asked, with no duplicate send.
13. pre_checkout answered without the LLM.
14. initData validation, including a stale auth_date.
15. A tainted run trying to email an untrusted address always produces an ask with a warning, even with an 'always' grant present.

Plus Sentinel table-driven unit tests and the invariant checks from 4.10.

==============================================================
14. PARALLEL BUILD PLAN (one session, many coding agents)
==============================================================
Phase 0 (blocking, one agent): contracts/, db schema + migrations + repos skeleton, kernel/, test fakes (FakeTelegram, ScriptedLLM, FakeClock), createApp wiring stubs.
Phase 1, in parallel:
- WS1 telegram: ingress, dispatcher lanes, outbox, DraftStreamer, render and sanitize, channels, topics.
- WS2 agent: requestBuilder, loop and state machine, stop reasons, fallback echo, context builder, epochs, prompt v1.
- WS3 trust: sentinel rules, taint and provenance, grants, approvals service and cards, callbackData codec.
- WS4 tools: executor, builtin tools (time, reminders, ledger, settings, approvals-revise), research tools.
- WS5 integrations: ComposioProvider + fake, oauth callback, triggers webhook, gmail/gcal/notion/todoist/drive ToolSpecs with reconcile().
- WS6 missions, watchers, scheduler, proactive engine.
- WS7 memory: store, retrieve, extract, forget, import; privacy (export, delete, shred, retention).
- WS8 business and guest channels, STT and voice pipeline, timezone resolver.
- WS9 Mini App frontend + /api + initData auth.
- WS10 billing (Stars).
Phase 2: the e2e golden scenarios and invariant suite (WS11 owns it), then integration fixes.

==============================================================
15. WALKTHROUGHS
==============================================================
A) 'Tell Alice I'm 10 min late', sent at 14:03.
1. The webhook writes to inbox; the dm lane writes conversation_inputs; a run is queued.
2. The worker appends the user message (seq 41) and the context message (seq 42), which contains gmail=act and memory [m_7 Alice Chen alice@x.com, sourced from the user's message on 3 Sep], so the target is trusted.
3. Draft status: 'Drafting email…'. The first assistant turn is tool_use gmail_create_draft.
4. S13 allows it; it executes with idem = toolu_…; the result is {draft_id}.
5. The next turn is tool_use gmail_send_draft. S99 says ask, so a pending action and a card are created, and the tool_result says pending_approval.
6. The final text reads 'Drafted, tap Approve to send', with the footer '⏳ 1 action awaiting your approval'. The run is done.
7. The user taps ✅, 2 minutes or 6 hours later.
8. CONTROL lane: HMAC and owner check, atomic transition, Sentinel re-check, execution of the stored payload.
9. The card is edited to '✅ Sent 14:05', the ledger is written, and an event goes into the next context.
10. Because this is the third approval to alice@x.com, the next card for her offers [♾ Always].

B) Mission: 'watch ALA→IST 20-27 Oct, tell me under $250, then hold it in my calendar'.
1. mission_start creates topic '✈️ ALA→IST fares' and the status card.
2. The run calls flight_search (Kiwi) and watcher_create(kind: flight, interval 6 h, condition price<250), then task_wait(on watcher:W3, timeout 14 d). The run parks.
3. Three days later a watcher hit wakes the run. It calls calendar_create_event (a hold, no attendees, R1).
4. The approval card appears in the mission topic. The user taps [⏱ 24h].
5. The event is created, the status card is ticked, mission_finish runs, and the topic is renamed '✅ ALA→IST fares'. The DM notice carries a deep link to book, and Gora states plainly that it cannot purchase.

tools.name: web_search
tools.purpose: Anthropic server tool web_search_20260209 (max_uses 5, blocked_domains list). For current facts, prices and news. Results are untrusted and taint the run. FULL and PUBLIC toolsets.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.purpose: Anthropic server tool web_fetch_20260209. Reads a specific page. Output is untrusted and taints the run. FULL and PUBLIC toolsets.

tools.name: time_resolve
tools.purpose: Deterministic date and time parsing and arithmetic with chrono-node in the user's IANA timezone. Returns ISO time, unix time and a human echo such as 'Tue 14 Oct, 15:00 Almaty'. The model must use it for every date it computes.

tools.name: weather_get
tools.purpose: Forecast and air quality from Open-Meteo, falling back to MET Norway. Used for briefs, trip planning and nudges about outdoor events.

tools.name: place_verify
tools.purpose: Checks that a venue or business exists and is open, with hours and a verified-at date, using OSM Nominatim/Photon, opening_hours tags and web_fetch of the official site. The system prompt requires it before any specific venue is recommended.

tools.name: fx_convert
tools.purpose: Currency conversion via open.er-api.com, which covers KZT and RUB. Rates are cached daily.

tools.name: flight_search
tools.purpose: Itinerary and price search through the Kiwi MCP search-flight tool, called client-side through @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and SentinelFetch. Returns options and booking deep links. Gora never buys tickets.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.purpose: Searches the user's own structured memory facts, scoped by conversation kind. Returns fact ids and their sources for citation and /why.

tools.name: memory_save
tools.purpose: Explicitly saves a durable fact the user shared, with its source message. Needs memory consent. Sensitive categories become pending_consent until the user confirms. Blocked while incognito.

tools.name: memory_forget
tools.purpose: Forgets specific facts or everything matching a query: tombstones them, records fingerprints and schedules epoch rotation. Runs directly when the user asks in an untainted turn; Sentinel asks first if the run is tainted.

tools.name: reminder_create
tools.purpose: Creates a one-off or recurring self-reminder (croner plus IANA timezone) with a date_time confirmation. It only notifies the owner.

tools.name: reminder_list
tools.purpose: Lists upcoming reminders.

tools.name: reminder_cancel
tools.purpose: Cancels or snoozes one of the user's reminders.

tools.name: mission_start
tools.purpose: Starts a durable background mission with a goal, success criteria, optional deadline and budget. Opens a private-chat topic and a status card. Quota-checked by Sentinel S06; the mission's own side effects are gated separately.

tools.name: mission_report
tools.purpose: Updates the mission status card (checklist, progress) and can post one progress message, rate-limited to one per mission per hour.

tools.name: mission_finish
tools.purpose: Completes a mission: posts the summary, renames the topic to show it is done, and sends a DM notice.

tools.name: task_wait
tools.purpose: Parks the current run until a time, an approval, a watcher hit or a user message. The tool_result is delivered on wake, so waits can last hours or days without holding resources.

tools.name: watcher_create
tools.purpose: Creates a page, price, flight, inbox or weather watcher with a condition and interval (quota-limited). It speaks only when the content hash changes and the condition is met.

tools.name: watcher_cancel
tools.purpose: Stops or pauses a watcher.

tools.name: ledger_query
tools.purpose: Read-only access to the user's ledger, so Gora can answer 'what did you do yesterday' or 'what did you read from my inbox' with sources.

tools.name: revise_pending_action
tools.purpose: Replaces a still-pending approval with a revised payload, e.g. after 'make it warmer'. The old card is marked superseded and a new card needs approval. The model has no tool that approves anything.

tools.name: integration_connect
tools.purpose: Sends a just-in-time Connect card (Composio Connect Link url button) for gmail, googlecalendar, notion, todoist or googledrive. It cannot set permission levels; those change only in the Mini App or through user callbacks.

tools.name: settings_update
tools.purpose: Updates the nudge budget, quiet hours, timezone, agent name/style, brief time and voice replies at the user's request. It cannot touch permissions, grants, connections or consents.

tools.name: gmail_search
tools.purpose: Searches the user's Gmail threads (permission level read or higher). Output is redacted (OTPs, magic links and reset links stripped), labeled untrusted, taints the run and is logged as a data read in the ledger.

tools.name: gmail_read_thread
tools.purpose: Reads one Gmail thread. Redacted, untrusted, and logged as a data read.

tools.name: gmail_create_draft
tools.purpose: Creates a Gmail draft visible in the user's mailbox (level draft or higher). This is phase one of the two-phase send: nothing leaves the mailbox.

tools.name: gmail_send_draft
