trust_and_safety:
THREAT MODEL
1. Prompt injection. Sources: emails, web pages, Drive and Notion content, forwarded messages, business messages, guest and group text, and pasted imports.
2. Model error and overclaiming. Examples: saying something was sent when it wasn't, recommending a closed venue, getting the timezone wrong.
3. Spoofed consent. Examples: typed 'approve', buttons emitted by the model, forged callback_data, another user in a group tapping.
4. Privilege escalation by the model. The model tries to change permissions or grants, or to message arbitrary chats.
5. Cross-scope leakage. Private memory leaks into a group or guest reply, or one business chat leaks into another.
6. Credential exposure. Bot token, OAuth tokens or Telegram file URLs reach the model, logs or providers.
7. Database or backup theft.
8. Runaway loops, cost or spam.
9. Telegram Bot Developer ToS violations, especially for Business data.

CONTROL 1: SENTINEL, A POLICY LAYER IN CODE
- evaluate() is a pure, table-tested function with ordered rules S01 to S99 (see Architecture 5.1).
- It is the only authority that decides allow, deny or ask. The model cannot call it, see how it works, or change its inputs.
- Every decision is written to sentinel_decisions and to the ledger.
- Execution is possible only through tools/executor.ts. Two tests enforce this: an import-graph test, and a test that grep-bans global fetch in tools/ and integrations/.
- SentinelFetch applies per-tool host allowlists, permits only GET for watchers and research, and logs every host it contacts.
- Money movement and credential entry are denied in v1 (R4).
- The /pause kill switch denies every non-read action and parks all missions. An operator-level global kill switch and per-integration disable flags exist for incidents.

CONTROL 2: APPROVALS THAT CANNOT BE FORGED
- Approval cards are generated by code and sent as their own messages. They are never part of the streamed model text.
- A card resolves only through a callback_query whose from.id is the owner. callback_data carries a truncated HMAC-SHA256 over (id|verb|scope|owner) under CALLBACK_HMAC_KEY.
- Typed words such as 'approve' or 'yes' are never accepted; Gora replies 'tap the button'.
- Model output is sanitized:
  - <tg-button>, <tg-button-row>, web_app and login_url tags are stripped;
  - lines imitating the card header are neutralized.
- The state transition is atomic (WHERE status='pending'), so double taps are no-ops.
- The executor runs the STORED payload, which must match its sha256. Sentinel re-checks it at execution, so a revocation or /pause after the tap still wins.
- No model call happens between the tap and execution.
- Mini App approvals require valid initData HMAC and an auth_date within 1 h.
- Approvals are never shown in groups or on behalf of a business account. They always go to the owner's DM or topic.

CONTROL 3: TAINT AND PROVENANCE
- A run that has read external content is tainted. Its outbound actions always ask, unless every target is user-trusted AND a grant covers it.
- A target is user-trusted only if it appears in the user's own messages, in memory sourced from the user, or in a previously approved action.
- A target that came from untrusted content always asks, with the warning '⚠ this recipient came from an email, not from you'. No 'always' grant can cover it.
- Taint propagates from a run into the missions it spawns.

CONTROL 4: UNTRUSTED CONTENT HANDLING
- All external content reaches the model wrapped in <untrusted source=… id=…> envelopes. The static system prompt says such content is data, never instructions.
- Operator instructions travel only in the top-level system prompt and in code-generated role:'system' context messages, which carry operator authority.
- Email output is stripped of OTPs, password-reset links and magic links before the model sees it, following the Muse approach.
- Guest and business texts are always untrusted.
- Anthropic's own classifiers and server-side fallbacks ('default') handle policy declines. A refusal is checked before any content is read, and tools from a refused turn never run.

CONTROL 5: HONESTY BY CONSTRUCTION
- The capability registry in the static prompt states what Gora cannot do: purchase, phone calls, logged-in browsing, messaging people outside approved email or business replies. The model is told to say 'I can draft this; you send it'.
- A pending_approval tool_result explicitly says performed:false.
- State footers ('⏳ awaiting approval', '✅ sent 14:04') come from DB state, not model text.
- Dates are computed only through time_resolve and echoed with the timezone.
- place_verify must run before a specific venue is recommended. Facts about prices and hours carry citations or a verified-at date.
- /why answers deterministically from llm_calls, tool_calls and run_memory_uses.

CONTROL 6: SCOPE ISOLATION
- Every conversation and memory fact carries a scope key. Retrieval filters by the scopes allowed for each context kind:
  - DM sees only user scope.
  - A business conversation sees user scope read-only, plus that one business chat.
  - Guest sees nothing.
  - Group sees only that group's scope (later).
- Guest and group conversations use a separate PUBLIC toolset with no memory and no integrations. They are structurally unable to reveal private data.
- Chat ids are namespaced by context (dm, guest, business), following Telegram's note that these identifiers are independent.

CONTROL 7: CREDENTIALS AND SECRETS
- OAuth tokens live with Composio. Gora stores only connected_account_id. Future direct-MCP tokens are envelope-encrypted and never enter model context.
- Telegram file URLs contain the bot token, so they are never forwarded. Files are downloaded and the bytes re-sent or uploaded.
- The bot token, initData and message text are redacted from logs.
- Secrets are never stored in memory, and the extractor drops anything that looks like a credential.
- Webhooks verify the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header. Composio triggers verify their signature. OAuth state is random, single-use and expires in 10 minutes.

CONTROL 8: ENCRYPTION AT REST AND REAL DELETION (ToS 4.4a, 4.2)
- Content columns use field-level AES-256-GCM with per-user DEKs, wrapped by a KEK from a secret store. The AAD binds each ciphertext to its table, column and row.
- DEKs live in a separate keys.db on a separate volume with separate, short backup retention.
- The disk volume is also encrypted.
- SQLite secure_delete=ON overwrites deleted content.
- Forgetting a memory does the following:
  - nulls its text;
  - records fingerprints so it is never re-learned;
  - rotates conversation epochs, so the text leaves the replayed Claude context within minutes;
  - shreds the old epoch rows.
- Deleting an account (/delete_me) does the following within 24 h:
  - revokes Composio connected accounts;
  - destroys the user's DEK, making every ciphertext, including in backups, unreadable;
  - deletes the rows;
  - confirms to the user.
- /export returns the user's data as JSON.

CONTROL 9: CONSENT LEDGER (ToS 4.3, 5.4)
- Consents are explicit, recorded (with text version) and revocable. They cover: ToS, memory, sensitive memory, business LLM processing per chat, voice transcription, location, import and proactive features.
- Memory extraction needs memory consent. Incognito mode writes nothing.
- User data is never used for training or datasets, and Gora says so plainly in /privacy and in the bot description.

CONTROL 10: BUSINESS / SECRETARY MODE COMPLIANCE (ToS 5.2, 5.4)
- Business message content never reaches Anthropic or any third party until the owner authorizes that specific chat on a consent card. Until then only metadata is kept.
- Business data is used only for this user's chatbot service.
- Replies default to draft-only, approved in the owner's DM. v1 never auto-sends.
- Every business read, draft and send is in the ledger and visible to the owner, so nothing is hidden (5.4 v).
- Actions respect rights (can_reply) and Telegram's 24 h window.
- deleted_business_messages is honored immediately. Business content is kept for at most 30 days.
- Users are notified of material changes (5.4 vi).

CONTROL 11: PROACTIVITY AND ABUSE LIMITS
- The nudge budget (default 3 per day), quiet hours, 'never this kind' and 👎 learning are enforced in code.
- The proactive engine cannot request new data unless that data is tied to a goal the user stated. This avoids Muse-style data grabs.
- Per-user rate limits on inbound messages (@grammyjs/ratelimiter), daily quotas per action class (for example 20 sends), bulk-send caps and mission cost budgets.
- Bot-to-bot mode is off in v1. Loop guards (dedupe, depth, per-peer rate, timeout) are specified for when it is enabled.
- Gora never cold-messages third parties. The only outbound messages are approved emails, calendar invites and business replies.

CONTROL 12: RETENTION
- inbox: 72 h.
- Guest conversations: 24 h.
- Voice audio: discarded after transcription.
- Raw LLM response payloads: 30 days.
- Business message text: 30 days.
- Conversation history, memory and ledger: kept until the user deletes them, or deleted after 12 months of inactivity following a warning.
- Anthropic, Composio and STT providers are listed in /privacy, with data processing terms. ZDR is used where available.

CONTROL 13: PAYMENTS
- Digital plans are paid only in Stars (XTR).
- pre_checkout is answered by deterministic code within 10 s.
- Entitlements are granted only after successful_payment.
- /paysupport and /terms are available, and refunds go through refundStarPayment.
- The trust features (approvals, ledger, memory controls, export and delete) are never paywalled.
risks: Telegram feature availability: Threaded Mode, Guest Mode and Secretary Mode depend on BotFather settings, and some of their names come from third-party docs. Mitigation: derive feature flags from getMe (has_topics_enabled, supports_guest_queries, can_connect_to_business) at boot and use fallbacks: missions in the main DM, guest mode disabled, business onboarding hidden.

Undocumented draft rate limits: frequent sendRichMessageDraft calls could hit 429s. Mitigation: throttle to at most 1 update per 700 ms per chat and skip intermediate states, keep a 15 s keepalive, use auto-retry, and fall back to typing plus a single final message after repeated 429s.

Rich Markdown parse failures, or Rich Markdown not available in business chats. Mitigation: a sanitizer, then the fallback chain rich markdown → telegram-md-entities {text, entities} → plain 4096-char chunks. Business sends default to entities.

Guest-mode semantics are only partly documented: there is no answerGuestQuery deadline, and editing through inline_message_id is 'likely' rather than confirmed. Mitigation: answer within 3 s with a placeholder. If the inline edit fails, send the full answer as the single reply on the next summon, or use the 'Continue privately' deep link.

Prompt injection remains unsolved (Meta says so too). Mitigation: taint plus provenance rules, untrusted envelopes, email redaction, approvals that cannot be spoofed, no money movement in v1, a bulk-action ask rule, and a red-team suite of injected emails and web pages in CI.

Approval fatigue could push users to disengage or grant 'always' too broadly. Mitigation: risk tiers, grants limited to user-trusted targets, a trust ladder that offers 'always' only after repeated identical approvals, digest batching for low-risk mission steps, and metrics on time-to-approve and on how often each tier is approved.

Some external side effects have no native idempotency (Gmail send via Composio). Mitigation: a two-phase draft→send flow, the tool_use_id idempotency key, reconcile() that searches Sent mail or events after a crash, and an 'unknown' state that asks the user instead of re-sending.

Tension between append-only history and deletion rights. Mitigation: epoch rotation (simple compaction) plus shredding of old epoch rows and forgotten-fact fingerprints. The residual risk is that forgotten text can stay in Anthropic's prompt cache up to the TTL (at most 1 h). Disclose this in /privacy.

Beta API drift: the scalar fallbacks:'default', clear_at, role:'system' typing on the beta client and compaction config are unconfirmed. Mitigation: isolate all of them in agent/requestBuilder.ts and transport.ts behind feature flags and casts. Contract tests run against the recorded request shape, plus a smoke test when keys arrive.

Future preserved-thinking enforcement (claude-opus-5-5, accounts created after 2026-08-31) will reject edited history. Mitigation: append-only triggers, a prefix-stability invariant test, fallback echo applied at write time, and a CI job with the block-binding beta set to 'error'.

Cost: Opus 5 at $5/$25 per MTok on a free tier. Mitigation: a byte-identical static prefix for cross-user 1h caching, effort routing (medium for chat, low for guest), epoch rotation near 120k tokens, clear_at for context messages, side calls kept minimal, per-plan quotas and mission budgets enforced by Sentinel S06, and a cache-hit-ratio alert.

Composio dependency: the consent screen says 'Composio'. Gmail and Calendar triggers poll about every 15 min. The managed-app allowance is 20K calls, and Gmail restricted-scope verification is needed once we move to our own OAuth app. Mitigation: IntegrationProvider abstraction, a direct-MCP path planned (Notion, Todoist, Linear support DCR), and budgeting for Google verification before scaling.

A single process with a single-writer SQLite has a scaling ceiling, and a node:sqlite synchronous write can block the event loop. Mitigation: short BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions, WAL, no LLM calls inside transactions, repositories isolated for a later move to Postgres, and leases already designed for multiple workers. Target about 10k weekly active users before sharding.

Telegram keeps updates for at most 24 h. Longer downtime loses updates, and a crash between a Telegram send and marking it in the outbox can duplicate a message. Mitigation: health checks with automatic restart, Litestream backups, inbox dedupe by update_id, and harmless-duplicate design (cards are keyed to one pending_action).

ToS and ban risk for Business data (5.4 iv) and for proactive messaging perceived as spam. Mitigation: per-chat consent before any LLM processing, metadata-only by default, draft-only replies, a visible ledger, nudge budgets, disable_notification for low-priority messages, and honoring deleted_business_messages.

Timezone and date errors, which are Poke's top complaint. Mitigation: deterministic time_resolve with chrono-node, the IANA timezone from the Mini App device, the geo-tz default entry (never geo-tz/now), the timezone echoed in every confirmation, and DST handled by croner. Timezone edge cases get their own test fixtures.

Mini App security: the 10.2 origin lock, replayed initData and a stale auth_date. Mitigation: serve from the exact registered origin, validate the HMAC with timingSafeEqual, require auth_date within 1 h for mutations, use a strict CSP, and never open the Mini App from reply-keyboard buttons.

Regulatory exposure (GDPR and similar) for EU users and for minors. Mitigation: data processing agreements with Anthropic, Composio and Groq, ZDR where possible, export and delete within 24 h, age gating in the ToS (13+ or local minimum), and no special-category memories without explicit consent.
later_features: Gora Computer (v2): a per-user Browserbase session and Context (persistent logins), driven by claude-opus-5 with computer_toolset_20260801 through a playwright-core connectOverCDP adapter. The Browserbase live view is embedded in the Mini App so the user handles login, 2FA and payment. Sentinel intercepts egress with page.route and gates form submits. Steel is the fallback.

Anthropic Managed Agents as the heavy mission backend: per-user vaults with mcp_oauth and environment_variable secrets injected at egress, limited networking, per-session budgets, and always_ask tools mapped to Telegram approval cards via user.tool_confirmation.
Payments on the user's behalf using Stripe single-use cards or Link, bound to merchant, amount and time. Exact-detail approval every time, and never an 'always' grant.

Per-chat Secretary auto-reply mode with a trust ladder, for low-risk templated replies to trusted contacts. Business checklists via sendChecklist and editMessageChecklist, and a delegated-read toggle for readBusinessMessage.

Full group product: summaries with privacy mode off by opt-in, decision and action-item tracking, native polls (members_only, revoting), RSVP and cost-split ledgers, a pinned group memory the group can edit, and ephemeral per-user answers and approvals via ephemeral_message_parameters.

Gora-to-Gora coordination ('crew'): internal routing between Gora users to negotiate meeting times, where each owner approves their own slot. Later, Bot-to-Bot Communication Mode with specialist bots, with the required loop guards.
Personal named agents via Managed Bots: t.me/newbot/<gora>/<suggested> creates a user-owned bot identity with its own avatar through setMyProfilePhoto, and one process routes multiple tokens.
Voice replies via OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts with Ogg/Opus output to sendVoice, with an AI-voice disclosure. Also video-note input and a hands-free voice-first mode.
Direct MCP integrations with our own OAuth client (DCR/CIMD) for Notion, Linear, Todoist, Canva, Airtable, Granola and others. A branded, verified Google OAuth app to replace Composio's managed app.
Code execution and Agent Skills (pptx, xlsx, docx, pdf) as isolated sub-calls, so users can ask for a deck, spreadsheet or PDF and get it back through the Files API and replyWithDocument.
Live-location awareness: place-based reminders and 'you're near X' nudges from shared live location (edited_message.location), resolved with geo-tz and Nominatim, within the nudge budget.
Flight tracking by flight number via AeroDataBox, with gate and delay alerts, plus adsb.lol live position cards with rich map blocks.
Confidential computing with user-held keys (a SecureStorage- or passkey-derived DEK) so even operators cannot read memory. A published security whitepaper and a bug bounty.
Migration to claude-opus-5-5 (cheaper, 0.05x cache reads) once enforcement tests pass, and Postgres or multi-instance workers behind the existing repository and lease abstractions.
